title: PPT template gift after Codex rounds 1 to 3 and the layout-override fix: notes to a deck in the company's own template, inside the browser
plain: A web page takes a company PowerPoint template and a plain-text outline and gives back an editable deck in that template, and after it has loaded it cannot send anything anywhere.
what_why:
The page in docs/ loads Python (Pyodide, python-pptx and the deckfill package) from its own folder. It then adds a second Content Security Policy that blocks fetch, XHR, beacons, image requests and new workers. From then on, the user's template, outline and deck stay in the tab.

The deckfill package does the work in three calls the page makes one at a time:
- read: check the template's size and package graph, then sort its layouts into title, content, two, section and other
- plan: turn the outline into slides, choose a layout for each, and split slides the fit estimate says are too full
- fill: remove the template's sample slides, add the planned slides into the layouts' own boxes, copy footers the template shows, and put the template's own bytes back for every part the fill did not mean to change

The same package runs under CPython in the tests, and the browser's download is byte for byte the CPython output (C10).
requirements: D1: static site in docs/, Python through self-hosted Pyodide on the main thread, one deckfill module with read_template, parse_outline, plan_deck, fill

D1b (rev 5): the template is untrusted: 100 MB file, 2,000 members, 150 MB uncompressed, 30 MB XML, 5 MB per XML part, 100:1 ratio, caps enforced on bytes actually read; safe XML parsing; the seat may lower a cap to meet C12
D3: layouts classed by type and placeholders, never by name; a slide may only use a layout with a destination for every need
D4: sample slides removed with everything only they reach; every other part kept; footers follow what the template already shows; no text outside a placeholder
D5: split, warned or marked 'check this slide' by a fit estimate
D6: no request to another origin; at ready the page locks the network off, and Python's fetches are covered
D8: Cantonese copy in one file; mentron.hk look; phone view explains and hands over the link

design.text: Three layers. The page (docs/app.js) owns the UI, the loading and the lockdown. It calls a small Python bridge (deckfill.web.Session) that turns each step into JSON. The deckfill package reads, plans and fills. Python runs on the main thread, because GitHub Pages cannot give a worker its own policy and a worker made from a URL does not inherit the page's lockdown. The page paints a working state and yields before every Python call, and the D1b caps bound the longest call.

decisions.decision: Kept parts go back as the template's own bytes when their meaning is unchanged
decisions.why: G0 showed python-pptx re-sorting relationships and relativising absolute targets on every real template (EDB, elderly.gov.hk, Microsoft, USC), which C3 flagged; fixtures made by python-pptx never showed it

decisions.decision: The restore step compares libxml2 serialisations, not C14N 2.0
decisions.why: C14N 2.0 in lxml is pure Python: a 5.6 s main-thread task on the elderly.gov.hk template against C12's 3 s bar; now 1.55 s

decisions.decision: Lockdown is a second CSP meta added at ready
decisions.why: D6; measured in Chromium: after it, fetch from JS and Python and new workers are blocked and the server sees nothing (qa/e2e/c9-report.json)

call_path.text: Everything is new in this build. Changed in fix round 1: the boot order (prompt before engine), the stale-plan guard around download, and the engine checks marked in steps 2 to 4. Changed in the layout-override fix: a pick is placed on its slide by title, kind and nth (step 6). Boxes link to the steps below.

implementation.title: Boot: the prompt first, then the engine, then the lockdown
implementation.text: boot loads prompt.txt and checks the HTTP status before anything else; a failure sets the retry state and stops, and retry runs boot again, so Copy is never enabled with no prompt behind it ([loadPromptText](docs/app.js#L129-L138)). Only then does loadEngine load Pyodide, the wheels and deckfill.zip (zipped from src/deckfill by [build_docs](scripts/build_docs.py#L1-L25)) from the page's own folder, import every module and append the lockdown policy ([lockdown](docs/app.js#L113-L118)). The base policy is the first meta in the head ([CSP](docs/index.html#L5-L5)); the only links out are three fixed anchors ([anchors](docs/index.html#L15-L16)); at 760 px or less the page shows the explainer and the copy-link button and skips the engine ([phone CSS](docs/style.css#L248-L268)). Fonts are self-hosted: [build_fonts](scripts/build_fonts.py#L1-L66) subsets Noto Serif TC to the glyphs the page's own strings use and Newsreader to Latin, and copies Mentron Serif. Every page string, the example outline included, sits in one copy file ([copy](docs/copy.js#L1-L126)); the prompt text ([prompt](docs/prompt.txt#L1-L29)) is the same text as [PROMPT.md](PROMPT.md#L1-L35) and the skill body ([skill](skill/ppt-outline/SKILL.md#L1-L34)), checked by [C14](tests/test_c14_copy.py#L1-L62); the [README](README.md#L1-L25) points to the page.

implementation.title: Read: preflight, caps, XML by content type, integrity
implementation.text: Before zipfile builds anything, preflight walks the central directory from the raw bytes. It reads the ZIP64 end records whenever their locator sits before the classic end record, whatever the classic fields hold, because zipfile does the same (Codex round 2, F3): over 2,000 records is too_big, a count that disagrees with the end record is bad_file. unzip then enforces the size caps on declared and actual bytes ([unzip](src/deckfill/package.py#L121-L133)). load treats a part as XML by name or by content type ([is_xml](src/deckfill/package.py#L229-L231)), holds every XML part to the XML caps and the safe parser ([load](src/deckfill/package.py#L328-L348)), and check_integrity now resolves the package root's relationships too ([root](src/deckfill/package.py#L307-L313)). The parser has entities, network, huge trees and DTD loading off, and any DOCTYPE is refused as bad_file ([xmlsafe](src/deckfill/xmlsafe.py#L25-L46)). read_template then classes each layout from its type and placeholders, never its name: a typed layout keeps its class only when it has the boxes that class needs, otherwise the placeholder rules decide, and anything left is other ([classify](src/deckfill/template.py#L293-L318)); each body box gets a fit model from its position, autofit and level styles, or none when the box is missing ([measure_body](src/deckfill/template.py#L242-L274)). Failures are codes the page maps to Cantonese messages ([errors](src/deckfill/errors.py#L1-L22)).

implementation.title: Plan: every body estimated, subtitles included
implementation.text: parse_outline refuses text over the character cap as too_long, normalises line ends and a BOM, then reads the # deck title, ## slides and indented bullets into slides with line-numbered warnings ([parse_outline](src/deckfill/outline.py#L63-L145)). plan_deck lists the compatible layouts per outline slide, takes the override when the slide fits it and the default otherwise ([fallback](src/deckfill/plan.py#L218-L247)), and splits bodies by the fit estimate. A title slide whose subtitle goes into a content body (the no-title-layout fallback, or an override) now gets that body's estimate: warned when it overflows, check when the box is not modelled. The wrap estimate counts a long word's lines with one division instead of one subtraction per line ([text_lines](src/deckfill/plan.py#L133-L170)).

implementation.title: Fill: sample slides out, footers placed, template bytes back
implementation.text: remove_slides strips every element that used a relationship to a removed slide, in parts python-pptx parses and, now, in XML parts it keeps as bytes such as viewProps.xml. footers_for copies an example footer onto the new slide; when the new layout has no box of that type, _place_footer keeps the footer's own position, else its layout's or master's ([place](src/deckfill/fill.py#L146-L179)). _restore_kept puts the template's own bytes back for every kept part whose meaning is unchanged, XML found by content type ([restore](src/deckfill/fill.py#L268-L304)), and the output must pass the same integrity check as the input.

implementation.title: Page state: no download from an older plan
implementation.text: Any change to the outline, a layout or the template calls staleNow: Download is disabled at once and the generation counter moves, so a plan that finishes for older input is dropped ([staleNow](docs/app.js#L241-L251), [gen check](docs/app.js#L272-L272)). On click, download reads the outline and the overrides and Session.fill plans and fills from exactly those in one Python call ([bridge](src/deckfill/web.py#L131-L140)), so even a click that lands mid-edit ships the text on screen.

implementation.title: Layout picks follow their slide
implementation.text: A pick in the layout list is stored as the slide's title, kind, nth (which of the slides with that title and kind it is) and count (how many slides share them) ([remember](docs/app.js#L324-L327)). The bridge computes nth and count for every slide ([groups](src/deckfill/web.py#L44-L54)). On every plan and every fill, place_overrides finds the nth slide with that title and kind in the outline it was given, so a slide added or removed above does not move the pick. A pick whose slide is gone, renamed or of another kind comes back as a layout_gone warning naming the old title. So does a pick whose group of same-titled slides changed size when either size is above one, because nth can no longer tell which slide it was; it is never moved to a sibling (Codex round 3, F16). plan_deck itself drops a pick the slide no longer fits, uses the default and adds layout_dropped; it also drops an index past the end with a blank layout_gone, which the page cannot send. The reply lists only the picks still in use ([kept](src/deckfill/web.py#L116-L122)), and the page replaces its own list with it, so a dropped pick's note shows once ([page](docs/app.js#L282-L282)). Before this, picks were keyed by slide index: after an insert above, the picked layout landed on the slide now at that index with no message (qa/override-fix/page-before.txt).

implementation.title: QA tooling: what each check proves
implementation.text: C9 runs one session through the real page on a local server ([server](tests/e2e/server.mjs#L1-L41)): two fills, an offline fill, then with the network back on a measured 30 s idle that must start after every download ([idle](tests/e2e/c9_privacy.mjs#L174-L185)), probes, then all three link-outs, each answered 204 so the page stays; the report records the commit and sha256 of every input and download, and [privacy_proof](qa/e2e/privacy_proof.py#L1-L54) fails on any request after ready, an idle that does not start after the last download or lasts under 30 s, or a changed tree. [C10](qa/e2e/c10_compare.py#L1-L48) compares the downloads part by part with CPython; [C1 page](tests/e2e/c1_edit_download.mjs#L1-L78), [F9](tests/e2e/f9_prompt_load.mjs#L1-L55) and [override](tests/e2e/override_follow.mjs#L1-L115) drive the three page fixes. [C12](tests/e2e/c12_load.mjs#L1-L192) throttles the network, reads Long Tasks and the wasm heap on the worst case [make_worst](qa/c12/make_worst.py#L1-L147) builds at both caps. [G0](qa/g0/run_g0.py#L1-L184) now gates on text outside placeholders through the [oracle](tests/oracle.py#L159-L177), whose C3 check takes out only the authorised link edits, then compares each kept part and its relationships as canonical XML, so order and target spelling count (F15) ([kept parts](tests/oracle.py#L265-L316)); goldens and fixtures come from [C1 tests](tests/test_c1_text.py#L1-L80) and [conftest](tests/conftest.py#L1-L32). [C15](qa/gemini/check_c15.py#L1-L91) needs all three cases and whole-number matches; the [validator runner](qa/c5/run_validator.py#L1-L104) needs every output in its [manifest](qa/c5/manifest.json#L1-L28) before it runs the [SDK tool](tools/validate/Program.cs#L1-L29); [D10](qa/demo/make_demo.py#L1-L69) builds the demo deck; [provenance](qa/provenance.py#L1-L30) stamps reports; [run_demos](qa/failure-demos/run_demos.py#L1-L114) mutates code and shows each check failing, its C9 runs in their own folders; [runner tests](tests/test_qa_runners.py#L1-L48).
